150.title: The Third Preaching Tour
150.b0.ask: “Why did a tour that made women teachers of the gospel and swept away superstition end in rejection at Jesus’ own home town of Nazareth?”
150.b2.p: The seventy-five or so evangelists who passed the test of experience on the second tour in Paper 149 now set out on a third. In January of A.D. 29, Abner and John’s apostles came to Bethsaida for a joint conference. John’s apostles wanted to make anointing the sick with oil a uniform practice for both groups, but Jesus declined to take part in the discussion, and his apostles refused to bind themselves by such a rule.
150.b3.p: The third mission lasted seven weeks. The evangelists went out in groups of five and covered Magdala, Tiberias, Nazareth, and all the principal towns of central and southern Galilee. Except for the northern regions, this was their last message to Galilee.
150.b4.p: On this tour the women’s evangelistic corps was formed for the first time, superstition was plainly exposed, and a simple answer was given to the question of salvation. Why, then, did it end with rejection by the people of Jesus’ home town?
150.b5.q: “⟦Q 150:5.5⟧You cannot buy salvation; you cannot earn righteousness. Salvation is the gift of God, and righteousness is the natural fruit of the spirit-born life of sonship in the kingdom.⟦/Q⟧”
150.b8.p: Of all the daring things Jesus did in his earth career, the most amazing was his sudden announcement on the evening of January 16: “⟦Q 150:1.1⟧On the morrow we will set apart ten women for the ministering work of the kingdom.⟦/Q⟧” These were women who had served at the former encampment and the tented infirmary. Later Mary Magdalene and Rebecca, the daughter of Joseph of Arimathea, were added, making twelve.
150.b9.t: Daughter of the former chazan of the Nazareth synagogue — their chief
Wife of Chuza, Herod’s steward — their treasurer
Daughter of a wealthy Jew of Tiberias and Sepphoris
Elder sister of Andrew and Peter
Sister-in-law of Jude, the Master’s brother in the flesh
Daughter of Elman, the Syrian physician
A cousin of the Apostle Thomas
150.b10.p: The women organized themselves, choosing Susanna as chief and Joanna as treasurer, and from then on they furnished their own funds. In a day when women were not even allowed on the main floor of the synagogue, this commission was the emancipation proclamation that set all women free for all time. The apostles were stunned and the whole country was stirred. The apostles practiced this recognition right after the Master’s departure, and in the early church women ministers were called deaconesses, but later generations fell back to the old customs.
150.b11.q: “⟦Q 150:1.3⟧in the kingdom of heaven there is neither rich nor poor, free nor bond, male nor female, all are equally the sons and daughters of God,⟦/Q⟧”
150.b13.p: Now any woman believer who wished to see the Master or the apostles could go to Susanna and, with one of the women evangelists, come straight into their presence. At Magdala the women first proved their usefulness. The apostles worked under strict rules about dealing with women, but the women evangelists were free to enter the evil resorts, preach the good news to all who lived there, and minister closely to their afflicted sisters.
150.b14.p: Through their ministry Mary Magdalene was won for the kingdom. A succession of misfortunes and society’s harsh treatment had left her in one of Magdala’s evil resorts, and it was Martha and Rachel who showed her that the doors of the kingdom were open even to her. Mary became the most effective teacher of the gospel among the women. And at the last tragic hour, when nearly all the apostles fled, these women were all present, and not one denied or betrayed him.
150.b16.p: The Sabbath service was placed in the women’s hands, and in the banquet room of Herod’s new palace Joanna read from the Scriptures about women’s work in Israel’s religious life — Miriam, Deborah, Esther, and others. That evening Andrew asked whether a new star was a sign that a great man had been born, and Jesus gave a thoroughgoing discussion of the whole subject of human superstition.
150.b17.t: The stars have nothing to do with human events; astronomy is a proper science
Reveals nothing about weather or the future
They do not come back to communicate with the living
Material things cannot influence the spiritual world
Pure material chance; it does not disclose the divine will
Lucky numbers and omens are unfounded superstition
A groundless system of fantastic speculation
Nothing more than the material they are made of
Derived from ancient superstitions, and futile
He exposed and denounced every enslaving superstition
150.b18.p: The only means of communion with the spiritual world lies in the spirit endowment of mankind: the indwelling spirit of the Father, the outpoured spirit of the Son, and the omnipresent influence of the Infinite Spirit.
150.b19.h: 4. Sending the Apostles out Two and Two
150.b20.p: “⟦Q 150:4.1⟧The harvest is plenteous, but the laborers are few,⟦/Q⟧” Jesus said. He stayed with the younger teachers and sent the twelve out two by two to cover all Galilee.
150.b22.p: On this mission, he said, they were not to go to gentile cities or Samaria but to the lost sheep of Israel, proclaiming the saving truth that man is a son of God. They need not fear those who can kill the body but cannot destroy the soul; not one sparrow is forgotten in God’s sight, and they were of more value than many sparrows. He also warned that when some in a family reject the gospel, division follows, so they should labor earnestly to save the whole family.
150.b23.h: 5. What Must I Do to Be Saved?
150.b24.p: At Shunem Rachel asked what they should answer when women asked, “⟦Q 150:5.1⟧What shall I do to be saved?⟦/Q⟧” Jesus said: believe this gospel of the kingdom, accept divine forgiveness, and by faith recognize the indwelling spirit of God, whose acceptance makes you a son of God. Entrance into the Father’s kingdom is wholly free, but growth in grace is essential to continuing in it.
150.b25.t: As Abraham was justified by faith
You partake of the divine nature and become a child of God
On the way of progressive and divine perfection
150.b26.p: Salvation is the gift of the Father, revealed by his Sons. We are not saved because we live righteously; we live righteously because we have already been saved and have recognized sonship. The realization of sonship is incompatible with the desire to sin. Those who heard went on with new power, and the women rejoiced all the more to know they were included in the plans for the kingdom.
150.b28.p: In the evenings Jesus spoke on many subjects — the love of God, dreams and visions, humility and meekness, music and worship, forgiveness in relation to repentance, doubts and unbelief, and more. With the older apostles away, the young men and women joined the discussions more freely. Jesus stayed two or three days with each group, and David’s messengers kept the scattered workers informed about one another, which greatly encouraged them. On Friday, March 4, they all gathered at Nazareth — Jesus’ first visit there since his public ministry began.
150.b30.p: Jesus walked through Nazareth unrecognized, past his childhood home, the carpenter shop, and the hill he had loved as a boy. Not since his baptism had such a flood of human emotion stirred in his soul. But Nazareth was not friendly. The townspeople resented that he had done no great works in the city of his youth, the younger generation was jealous of his fame, and his enemies had hired rough men to make trouble.
150.b32.p: On the Sabbath all Nazareth crowded into the synagogue. The roll handed to Jesus was the very manuscript he had given the synagogue as a young man, though no one remembered. The service followed the old form — prayers, the Shema, and the benedictions — with only the first and last benedictions recited to give the guest more time.
150.b33.p: Jesus read from Deuteronomy that the word of life is not in heaven or beyond the sea but very near, in your heart, and from Isaiah that the spirit of the Lord had anointed him to preach good tidings to the poor. Then he said, “⟦Q 150:8.10⟧Today are these Scriptures fulfilled,⟦/Q⟧” and spoke for almost fifteen minutes on “⟦Q 150:1.3|150:8.10|54:2.1⟧The Sons and Daughters of God.⟦/Q⟧” Afterward a crowd pressed forward with questions, and among them were men bent on mischief.
150.b35.p: To their rude questions and taunts Jesus answered half humorously that a prophet is not without honor except in his own country. When they demanded wonders, he said that the transformations of grace are wrought in response to the living faith of those who receive them.
150.b36.p: Jesus could have calmed the crowd good-naturedly, but Simon Zelotes gathered friends and took a belligerent stand, which stirred up the spirit of a mob. The ruffians dragged Jesus to the brow of a cliff to push him over. Just then he turned, faced them, and quietly folded his arms. When he began to walk forward, the mob parted and let him pass.
150.b37.p: This turbulent ending sobered all his followers. They were awakening to the fact that the kingdom would come only through much sorrow and bitter disappointment, and they gathered again at Bethsaida not as triumphant crusaders but as a sober and serious group of disillusioned preachers.
150.b39.p: Paper 150 is a journey in which the gospel crossed old boundaries. Women became official teachers of the gospel for the first time and carried the good news where the apostles could not go. Jesus cleared away the superstitions of stars, charms, and dreams, teaching that true communion with the spiritual world lies in the indwelling spirit. Salvation cannot be bought or earned; it is the Father’s gift received by faith, and a righteous life is its fruit. Yet the tour ended in rejection at Nazareth and a crisis at the edge of a cliff. Through it the disciples learned that the kingdom is built not amid applause but in an earnest faith that endures disappointment.
