Key message
The Women’s Evangelistic Corps
Commissioning women as teachers set all women free for all time
The Stop at Magdala
Through the women’s ministry Mary Magdalene entered the kingdom
Sabbath at Tiberias
Superstition swept away: communion with the spirit lies in the spirit endowment
Sending the Apostles out Two and Two
Fear not; you are of more value than many sparrows
What Must I Do to Be Saved?
Salvation is a gift, and righteousness is the fruit of the reborn life
The Evening Lessons
Young men and women freely discussed many subjects with the Master
The Sojourn at Nazareth
His home town met the former carpenter with hostility
The Sabbath Service
The word of life is near, in your heart, and fulfilled today
The Nazareth Rejection
The kingdom comes only through sorrow and disappointment
150.b42.box: Salvation is the Father’s gift received by faith, and the kingdom is built through an earnest faith that endures disappointment.
151.title: Tarrying and Teaching by the Seaside
151.b0.ask: “Why did Jesus begin teaching in parables at this time, and how should a parable be read?”
151.b2.p: After the rejection at Nazareth in Paper 150, all the preaching and teaching groups gathered again at Bethsaida by March 10. That Saturday night Jesus spoke for more than an hour on “⟦Q 151:0.1⟧The mission of adversity and the spiritual value of disappointment,⟦/Q⟧” and his hearers never forgot the lesson.
151.b3.p: Jesus had not fully recovered from the sorrow of Nazareth, and the apostles noticed a peculiar sadness mingled with his usual cheerfulness. While they waited to go up to Jerusalem for the Passover, the women went from house to house in Capernaum and the nearby towns, teaching the gospel and caring for the sick.
151.b4.p: In this period Jesus first began teaching the multitudes in parables. Why did he teach through stories? And how should we read those stories?
151.b5.q: “⟦Q 151:3.1⟧Think not only of the multitudes and how they hear the truth; take heed also to yourselves how you hear.⟦/Q⟧”
151.b8.p: One Sunday morning, as Jesus sat alone in the old fishing boat by the shore, nearly a thousand people gathered. When Peter asked whether he should speak to them, Jesus answered, “⟦Q 151:1.1⟧No, Peter, I will tell them a story,⟦/Q⟧” and he told the parable of the sower.
151.b9.t: Trodden underfoot and devoured by the birds
On rocky places with little earth
Sprang up quickly but withered in the sun for lack of root
Choked, so that it yielded no grain
Yielded thirtyfold, sixtyfold, and a hundredfold
151.b10.p: The apostles were perplexed, and Matthew asked why he spoke in parables. Jesus answered that those who truly wished to enter the kingdom would discern the meaning, while those who listened only to ensnare him would hear without understanding. It is the law of the spirit that to him who has, more shall be given, and from him who has not, even what he has shall be taken away.
151.b12.p: Peter and Nathaniel each assumed that every feature of the parable had a hidden meaning, and each offered an interpretation. To Peter the birds were Satan; to Nathaniel they were one’s habits of life, the temptation of evil, and the desires of the flesh. The apostles split almost evenly and fell into heated debate.
151.b13.p: Jesus let the confusion reach its height and then called them together. Thomas reminded them that the Master had told them not to make a spiritual application of every minor detail of a story. The proof, he said, was that an hour earlier they had all been of one mind, and now they were divided into two camps. The parable, Thomas said, taught one great truth: however faithfully they taught the gospel, the results would vary with conditions over which they had little or no control.
151.b14.t: An allegory, giving a meaning to every feature
The one central truth the whole parable teaches
151.b15.p: Jesus praised Thomas for discerning the true meaning of parables, and said that Peter and Nathaniel had done everyone equal good by showing so clearly the danger of making allegories out of his parables. Such flights of imagination may be enjoyed privately, but it is a mistake to offer them as public teaching.
151.b17.p: The next evening Jesus explained that before an audience of many different minds, a story lets each person interpret the teaching according to his own intellectual and spiritual endowments. No one lights a lamp and hides it under a vessel; they should let their light shine with wisdom and discretion. He advised against fables and allegories but encouraged the free use of parables, especially nature parables. He often called the natural “⟦Q 151:3.3⟧the unreal and fleeting shadow of spirit realities.⟦/Q⟧”
151.b18.t: Appeals to many levels at once
Stirs imagination and wins sympathy without arousing antagonism
From the known to the unknown
Uses the natural to introduce the spiritual
Evades prejudice and puts new truth gracefully into the mind
Rejecting it means consciously going against one’s honest judgment
Presents new truth without clashing with tradition and authority
Familiar scenes bring the lesson back to mind
151.b19.p: The parable of the sower was a review of his ministry so far and a forecast of what lay ahead, and a hint of what his messengers might expect in every generation. Parables drawn from nature were also the best answer to the charge that his work was done with the help of devils, and they gave his enemies less opportunity to accuse him. Finally he added a short parable of seed that grows by itself until harvest, but he never explained it further.
151.b21.p: The next day Jesus again taught from the boat in a series of parables. From this time on he seldom taught the masses except in parables, explaining them more fully to the apostles and evangelists in the evening classes.
151.b22.t: The kingdom of heaven is like…
Weeds sown by an enemy grow with the wheat until the harvest
The least of seeds becomes a tree where birds can rest
Leaven hidden in three measures of meal leavens the whole
A man sells all he has to buy the field
A merchant sells everything to buy one pearl of great price
A net gathers every kind of fish, and the good are sorted from the bad
151.b24.p: As the crowds kept growing, Jesus said, “⟦Q 151:5.1⟧I am weary of the throngs; let us cross over to the other side that we may rest for a day.⟦/Q⟧” On the way they met one of the sudden evening windstorms typical of the Sea of Galilee, caused when cool air from the gorges rushes down onto the lake, which lies far below sea level.
151.b25.p: Jesus, worn out, was asleep in the stern, and when the boat began filling with water, Peter shook him awake. Jesus said, “⟦Q 151:5.5⟧Where is your faith? Peace, be quiet,⟦/Q⟧” and almost at once the storm died down. The paper says this was purely coincidental as far as can be judged. Jesus explained that he had spoken to their fear-tossed minds, not commanded the elements, yet the apostles always regarded it as a nature miracle.
151.b26.q: “⟦Q 151:5.5⟧Why are all of you so filled with fear? Where is your faith? Peace, be quiet.⟦/Q⟧”
151.b28.p: Among the tomb caves near Kheresa lived Amos, a man afflicted with periodic insanity. In a lucid interval he had heard the preaching at Bethsaida and become a halfhearted believer. He believed his torment came from evil spirits, but the paper says his troubles were mostly emotional. Jesus took him by the hand, raised him up, and said, “⟦Q 151:6.5⟧Amos, you are not possessed of a devil,⟦/Q⟧” commanding him to come out of his spell, and Amos was immediately restored to his right mind.
151.b29.p: Meanwhile dogs charged a small, untended herd of swine and drove most of them over a cliff into the sea. From this incidental event arose the legend that a legion of devils had gone from Amos into the swine, and all the apostles except Thomas believed it. Amos believed it too, and that belief had much to do with the permanency of his cure. The swine-raising gentiles asked Jesus to leave, and when Amos begged to go with him, Jesus told him to return to his people and show them what great things God had done for him. Amos went through all the cities of the Decapolis telling of it.
151.b31.p: Paper 151 marks a turning point in how Jesus taught. Amid the rejection at Nazareth and the plotting of his enemies, he began to convey truth through stories drawn from nature. A parable opens itself to each hearer according to his capacity, and it plants a truth that an honest mind finds hard to reject while avoiding needless controversy. But as Thomas reminded them, giving a meaning to every detail only divides those who were once of one mind. The stories of the storm and the swine of Kheresa teach the same lesson: rather than inflate coincidences into miracles, we should attend to the peace given to fearful hearts and to the faith that knows we are sons of God.
151.b32.t: From this time Jesus began teaching the crowds in parables
A parable teaches one central truth, not a meaning in every detail
Parables let each person receive truth according to his capacity
Mustard seed, leaven, treasure, and pearl picture the kingdom
Jesus spoke peace not to the storm but to fearful hearts
You are not possessed of a devil; you are a son of God
151.b34.box: A parable teaches one great truth, and we must look not to how others hear but to how we ourselves hear.
152.title: Events Leading up to the Capernaum Crisis
152.b0.ask: “Why did the five thousand who had eaten their fill try to make Jesus king — and why did he refuse the crown?”
152.b2.p: News of the healing of Amos at Kheresa in Paper 151 had already reached Bethsaida and Capernaum, so a great crowd was waiting when Jesus’ boat came back. Among them were new observers from the Sanhedrin, looking for grounds to arrest him.
152.b3.p: On the way to the house of Jairus, a ruler of the synagogue, Jesus stopped and said, “⟦Q 152:0.2⟧Someone touched me,⟦/Q⟧” for he perceived that living energy had gone forth from him. Veronica, who had suffered for years from a hemorrhage, had touched the border of his garment and been healed. Jesus called her forward and said, “⟦Q 152:0.3⟧Daughter, your faith has made you whole.⟦/Q⟧” It was her faith, not her touch, that healed her, and Jesus did not want anyone to think that her fear in trying to steal a cure, or her superstition about his garment, had been honored.
152.b4.p: At this moment, when his fame as a healer was at its height, did the wonders lead people into the kingdom? This paper shows how that question played out in the feeding of the five thousand and the attempt to make him king.
152.b5.q: “⟦Q 152:3.2⟧If you must have a king, let the Father of lights be enthroned in the heart of each of you as the spirit Ruler of all things.⟦/Q⟧”
152.b8.p: Even after word came that the daughter had died, Jesus said, “⟦Q 152:1.1⟧Fear not; only believe.⟦/Q⟧” He put out the noisy mourners, took the girl by the hand, and said, “⟦Q 152:1.1⟧Daughter, I say to you, awake and arise!⟦/Q⟧” At once she got up and walked. Jesus explained to the family and the apostles that she had been in a coma after a long fever and that he had only awakened her, not raised her from the dead. But the apostles were miracle-minded, and all of them believed he had raised her from death.
152.b9.p: Jesus’ reputation as a healer was now at its very height, and he looked much worn. Never again, anywhere in this universe, will a being appear in mortal flesh while embodying the attributes of creative energy, so neither science nor religion can ever check these events. Yet by going away, Jesus made it possible for his spirit to live alongside the Father’s spirit in the minds of all mankind, and we should place no limit on the possible exhibition of his spiritual power.
152.b11.p: Jesus and the twelve crossed the lake to rest in a park south of Bethsaida-Julias, but the people hired boats or walked around the lake to follow. By Wednesday noon about five thousand had gathered, and by the third day the food they had brought was nearly gone. It was quietly whispered that Jesus had chosen this spot, beyond the reach of his enemies, to be crowned king, and even the apostles were divided.
152.b12.t: Peter, John, Simon Zelotes, Judas Iscariot
Joab, one of the young evangelists
152.b13.p: Philip and Andrew urged him to send the crowd away to buy food, but Jesus did not want to send them away hungry, like sheep without a shepherd. All that remained was what the Mark lad had: five barley loaves and two dried fishes. Jesus had the people sit in companies of a hundred, gave thanks, and broke the bread. All ate and were filled, and twelve baskets of fragments were left over.
152.b14.q: ⟦Q 152:2.10⟧And this is the first and only nature miracle which Jesus performed as a result of his conscious preplanning.⟦/Q⟧
152.b15.p: The paper explains that Michael multiplied the food elements as he always does, except that the time factor and the visible life channel were eliminated.
152.b17.p: This was another case where human pity plus creative power produced what happened. The people had long been taught that the Messiah would give them the bread of life as manna was given in the wilderness, and to them the power to feed carried the right to rule. As one man they shouted, “⟦Q 152:2.5|152:3.1|97:9.3⟧Make him king!⟦/Q⟧”
152.b18.p: Jesus stepped onto a huge stone and told them they meant well but were shortsighted and material-minded: they wanted to make him king not because their souls had been lighted with truth but because their stomachs had been filled with bread. The kingdom of heaven is a spiritual brotherhood, and no one rules over it from a material throne. The crowd went away stunned, and many followed him no more from that day. Only the Mark lad spoke: “⟦Q 152:3.3⟧And he refused to be our king.⟦/Q⟧”
152.b20.p: Rowing back without Jesus, the apostles struggled against a strong contrary wind, and Peter, the most downcast of them all, fell asleep exhausted. He dreamed that Jesus came walking on the sea and said, “⟦Q 152:4.2⟧Be of good cheer; it is I; be not afraid.⟦/Q⟧” In the dream he began to walk on the water, started to sink, and cried, “⟦Q 152:4.2⟧Lord, save me!⟦/Q⟧” — and he actually stepped overboard, waking as his companions pulled him out of the sea.
152.b21.p: To Peter this experience was always real. John Mark was only partly convinced and left part of the story out, while Luke, after careful inquiry, concluded it was Peter’s vision and left it out of his narrative.
152.b23.p: Jesus walked back to Bethsaida during the night with the Mark lad. Of the five thousand who were fed — their stomachs full and their hearts empty — only about five hundred kept following him. Jesus gathered the apostles and their associates and rebuked their slowness of spiritual understanding. Miracles and material wonders do not win souls for the spiritual kingdom. The crowd, once fed, did not hunger for the bread of life; they wanted a king so they could go on eating bread without toil.
152.b24.p: The episode brought to a head the apostles’ craving for miracles and for a king, and it ended the early era of teaching and healing, preparing the way for the last year of proclaiming the more spiritual phases of the gospel.
152.b26.p: While they rested at Gennesaret, Jesus’ open followers, who had numbered more than fifty thousand in Galilee alone, shrank in less than a month to fewer than five hundred. Jesus wanted his apostles to learn for themselves how fickle popular acclaim is. He told them the parable of the sower again and taught them what kind of appeal truly bears fruit.
152.b27.t: Transitory and utterly disappointing — useful only to arrest attention
Empty and barren — the mind is the gateway to the soul
Lasting success and marvelous transformations of character
152.b28.p: The apostles began to realize more fully that Jesus would not sit on David’s throne and that spiritual truth would not be advanced by material wonders. They saw that the feeding of the five thousand had been the height of popular acclaim, and they dimly foresaw the coming times of spiritual sifting. Jesus assured them that he had yielded to his sympathy for the multitude only after he had ascertained that it was “⟦Q 152:6.6⟧according to the Father’s will.⟦/Q⟧”
152.b30.p: On April 3 Jesus set out for Jerusalem with only the twelve, avoiding the crowds, and he forbade any public teaching on the journey or during their stay. He entered Jerusalem only once during this Passover, and the apostles, seeing how bitter feeling toward their Master had become, left convinced that a crisis was impending. Back in Bethsaida on April 29, Jesus sent Andrew to ask permission to speak in the Capernaum synagogue, knowing it would be the last time he would be allowed to do so.
152.b32.p: Paper 152 shows both the peak of Jesus’ popularity and its collapse. Veronica’s healing reveals that it is faith, not the touch of a garment, that makes whole; the feeding of the five thousand reveals that people with full stomachs do not necessarily seek the bread of life. When the crowd tried to make him king, Jesus refused a material throne and told them to enthrone the Father in each of their hearts. His followers dwindled from fifty thousand to five hundred, but the apostles began to learn that true transformation comes not from appeals to emotion or from miracles but from appeal to the spirit within. This paper stands at the threshold of the Capernaum crisis and the final year.
152.b33.t: It is living faith, not a touch, that heals
The first and only nature miracle Jesus planned beforehand
The kingdom is a spiritual brotherhood with no material throne
The walk on the water was Peter’s dream
Miracles do not win souls for the spiritual kingdom
Appeal not to feeling or intellect alone but to the spirit within
The apostles returned convinced that a crisis was impending
152.b35.box: Stomachs filled with bread want a king, but a soul lighted with truth enthrones the Father in the heart.
153.title: The Crisis at Capernaum
153.b0.ask: “Why did Jesus himself turn back the tide of popular enthusiasm, and set people face to face with a choice before the bread of life?”
153.b2.p: In Paper 152 Jesus refused the crown that the five thousand pressed upon him, and then went up to Jerusalem and back. On the Friday evening of their return to Bethsaida, and again on Sabbath morning, the apostles saw that he was deeply occupied with some momentous problem. He ate no breakfast and but little at noontide, and a suspense of apprehension rested upon them all.
153.b3.p: Nathaniel said they were in the “⟦Q 153:0.2⟧lull before the storm.⟦/Q⟧” Thomas felt that something out of the ordinary was about to happen. Simon Zelotes hoped the Father would intervene, and Judas Iscariot wondered whether Jesus regretted lacking the courage to let himself be made king. From among such depressed and disconsolate followers, Jesus went forth to preach his epoch-making sermon in the Capernaum synagogue.
153.b4.p: Why did Jesus so deliberately turn back the enthusiasm of the crowds? And what choice did that sermon force upon those who heard it?
153.b5.q: “⟦Q 153:5.4⟧It is the spirit that quickens; the flesh and all that pertains thereto is of little profit. The words which I have spoken to you are spirit and life.⟦/Q⟧”
153.b8.p: At three o’clock on that Sabbath afternoon, with Jairus presiding, the new Capernaum synagogue held a distinguished congregation: fifty-three Pharisees and Sadducees from Jerusalem, more than thirty leaders of the neighboring synagogues, and the official observers of Herod Antipas. These men were the orthodox vanguard, come to open warfare on Jesus and his disciples. The Jerusalem leaders had pleaded with Jairus to keep Jesus from speaking, but Jairus answered that he had granted the request and would not break his word.
153.b9.p: Jesus chose boldly to take the offensive. This sermon was the turning point from the period of discussion, controversy, and decision to that of open warfare and final acceptance or final rejection. Jesus understood that people prepare for the decisions of a crisis through the slow process of choosing again and again between good and evil, and so he had given his apostles repeated rehearsals in disappointment.
153.b10.t: From the feeding of the five thousand to this sermon in the synagogue
From this sermon for a whole year, until the Master’s trial and crucifixion
153.b11.p: One question filled every mind, friend and foe alike: why had he himself turned back the tide of popular enthusiasm? The disappointment of his disgruntled followers grew into opposition and at last into hatred. It was after this sermon that Judas Iscariot first consciously thought of deserting the Master.
153.b13.p: Jesus read from Deuteronomy the warnings of what would befall a people who would not hearken to the voice of God, and then the story of Jeremiah, who was let down into a filthy dungeon for warning his people. What, he asked, would the religious leaders of today do with the man who dared to warn them of their spiritual doom? They already had evidence enough to decide, and he told them, as Joshua had told their forefathers, “⟦Q 153:2.5⟧choose you this day whom you will serve.⟦/Q⟧”
153.b14.p: Some had hired boats to follow him, not for truth but for more bread for which they had not labored. Jesus told them not to hanker after food that perishes but to seek the spiritual food that nourishes to eternal life, for the work of God is to believe the one whom he has sent. Pointing to the pot of manna carved on the lintel of the synagogue, he declared that the manna in the wilderness was the bread of earth, and that the Father now offered them the true bread of life.
153.b15.q: “⟦Q 153:2.8⟧I am this bread of life. He who comes to me shall not hunger, while he who believes me shall never thirst.⟦/Q⟧”
153.b16.t: What kind of bread it is
Bread of earth — those who ate it are dead
Jesus’ own living nature, uniting God and man
153.b17.p: A member of the Sanhedrin challenged him: how could the son of Joseph the carpenter claim to have come down from heaven? Jesus asked for patience, saying, “⟦Q 153:2.11⟧the truth never suffers from honest examination.⟦/Q⟧” Everyone who yields to the teaching of the Father’s indwelling spirit will eventually come to him. The bread of life he gives the world is this revelation: the Father in the Son, and the Son one with the Father. The crowd did not finally disperse until well past seven o’clock.
153.b19.p: A Pharisee shouted from a lampstand, asking how Jesus could give them his flesh to eat and his blood to drink. Jesus answered that it was not his flesh and blood but his life in the flesh that is a bestowal of the bread of heaven. We can become one in spirit with him and be watered in soul by the divine spirit, which is truly the water of life.
153.b20.p: A spy from Jerusalem complained that Jesus and his apostles did not wash their hands before eating. Jesus pointed to the tradition that let undutiful children escape supporting their parents by declaring their money “⟦Q 153:3.3⟧given to God,⟦/Q⟧” and asked why they made void the commandment of God by their own tradition. Then he spoke to everyone present.
153.b21.t: What does not defile a man
That which enters into the mouth
That which proceeds out of the mouth and from the heart
Bread eaten with ceremonially unclean hands
Evil thoughts, wicked projects of murder, theft, and adulteries
What reaches the mind through the eyes and ears
Jealousy, pride, anger, revenge, railings, and false witness
153.b22.p: The traditionalists of that day held eating with unwashed hands to be an offense deserving excommunication. Even Peter, many years later, was freed from his fear of things clean and unclean only through an extraordinary and vivid dream. Knowing that an open rupture with the religious leaders could no longer be prevented, Jesus exposed the folly of the whole rabbinic system of the oral law.
153.b24.p: A Pharisee brought Jesus a youth possessed of an unruly and rebellious spirit. Moved with compassion, Jesus took him by the hand and commanded the spirit to come out of him, and at once the lad was in his right mind. The book explains that this was the first case where Jesus really cast an evil spirit out of a human being, and that after Pentecost, when the Master’s spirit was poured out upon all flesh, such possession became forever impossible.
153.b25.p: When a Pharisee charged that Jesus worked by the power of Beelzebub, Jesus answered that a kingdom divided against itself cannot stand. Then he gave a solemn warning: those who knowingly and with wicked intention ascribe the works of God to the doings of devils are guilty of eternally rejecting divine forgiveness. As each one now chooses, so shall he eventually be, for the tree is known by its fruits.
153.b26.q: “⟦Q 153:4.4⟧And as you now choose, so shall you eventually be.⟦/Q⟧”
153.b27.p: When another demanded a sign agreed upon in advance, Jesus replied that a faithless and sign-seeking generation would receive no sign but what it already had, and what it would see when the Son of Man departed. Amazed at so militant a Master, the apostles led him from the synagogue and walked home with him in silence.
153.b29.p: The sudden desertion of the crowds, the boldness of the Pharisees, and the Master’s change of tactics all came at once, and the apostles were badly shaken. Jesus would not eat and stayed alone for hours in an upper room. Joab reported that about one third of the evangelists had deserted. Meanwhile the twelve women met at Peter’s house; they were tremendously upset, but none of them deserted.
153.b30.p: A little after midnight Jesus came down and stood among about thirty of his followers. This sifting of the kingdom, he said, was unavoidable; the kingdom was being divested of its lukewarm multitudes and halfhearted disciples. Would they also desert? Let each look to his own faith, for one of them stood in grave danger.
153.b31.q: “⟦Q 153:5.4⟧You have taught us the words of eternal life. We have believed in you and followed with you all this time.⟦/Q⟧”
153.b32.p: As Peter finished his pledge of loyalty, they all with one accord nodded their approval. Jesus told them to go to their rest, for active days were just ahead.
153.b34.p: Paper 153 records the day on which Jesus’ public life changed course. To crowds who expected a material Messiah he offered not loaves but himself, the bread of life. In place of the tradition of washing hands, he taught that what defiles a man comes out of the heart. And he solemnly warned against the deliberate malice that ascribes the works of God to the devil. Many left him as a result, yet for Jesus this was not failure but an unavoidable sifting. We prepare for the decisions of a crisis through many small, repeated choices, and as we now choose, so we shall eventually be. That night Peter and the apostles held fast to the words of eternal life and chose to stay.
153.b35.t: This sermon was the turning point toward open warfare and final choice
Jesus offered not the bread of earth but the bread of life
What defiles a man is not his hands but what comes from his heart
As you now choose, so shall you be; the tree is known by its fruits
Even in the sifting, the apostles held fast to the words of eternal life
153.b37.box: It is the spirit that quickens, and before the bread of life each person becomes what he now chooses.
154.title: Last Days at Capernaum
154.b0.ask: “When the synagogue, the crowds, and even his own family turned away from him, whom did Jesus call his true family?”
154.b2.p: After the synagogue sermon of Paper 153, on that Saturday night of April 30, at the very hour when Jesus was comforting his downcast disciples, Herod Antipas was meeting at Tiberias with commissioners from the Jerusalem Sanhedrin. They urged him to arrest Jesus as a stirrer-up of rebellion, but Herod refused to act against him as a political offender.
154.b3.p: Chuza, one of Herod’s officials, had told him that Jesus had no intention of meddling with earthly rule and cared only for establishing the spiritual brotherhood of his believers. Troubled by a bad conscience for having put John the Baptist to death, Herod chose not to interfere, and when the Jews threatened to report him to Caesar, he ordered them out of his council chamber.
154.b4.p: Yet in less than a month everything was reversed. The synagogues were closed, Herod authorized the arrest, and even Jesus’ family came to take him home. At the place where all of this collapsed, whom did Jesus call his family?
154.b5.q: “⟦Q 154:6.5⟧For whosoever does the will of my Father who is in heaven, the same is my mother, my brother, and my sister.⟦/Q⟧”
154.b8.p: From May 1 to May 7 Jesus held intimate counsel at the Zebedee house with his tried and trusted disciples, meeting them morning, afternoon, and evening. Only about one hundred of them had the moral courage to brave the Pharisees and openly declare their adherence to him. On the Friday of that week the rulers of the Capernaum synagogue closed the house of God to Jesus and all his followers, and Jairus resigned as chief ruler and openly took his stand with Jesus.
154.b9.p: At the last seaside meeting, on May 7, fewer than one hundred and fifty gathered. This was the lowest ebb in the tide of popular regard for Jesus, yet from then on a slow but more healthful growth began, and a new following arose that was better grounded in spiritual faith. The compromising transition stage between the material and the spiritual ideas of the kingdom had now definitely ended.
154.b11.p: On May 8 the Sanhedrin passed an unprecedented decree closing all the synagogues of Palestine to Jesus and his followers. Until then each synagogue had been an independent congregation of worshipers, and five members of the Sanhedrin resigned in protest. Within two weeks every synagogue had bowed to the decree except the one at Hebron, which refused on the ground of congregational autonomy; shortly afterward it was destroyed by fire.
154.b12.p: That same day Jesus declared a week’s holiday and sent his disciples home to rest. During that week Nathaniel and James Zebedee suffered from a painful digestive disturbance. Jesus nursed them through the night, but he did not heal them supernaturally. Never once in his life on earth did he perform any supernatural ministration for a member of his earth family or for any of his immediate followers.
154.b13.q: ⟦Q 154:2.5⟧Problematic situations, coupled with exertion stimuli, conspire to produce those activities of mind, soul, and spirit⟦/Q⟧
154.b14.p: For the souls of mortals to grow and be perfected, universe difficulties must be met and planetary obstacles must be encountered. Will creatures do not progress favorably in environmental ease.
154.b16.p: At the second Tiberias conference, on May 16, the Jewish leaders reported that practically all the synagogues were now closed to Jesus. Herod still refused to arrest him himself, but he agreed to let the Sanhedrin seize Jesus and carry him to Jerusalem for trial on religious charges, provided the Roman ruler of Judea concurred.
154.b17.p: On the night of May 21 word came that the Jerusalem authorities had no objection, and just before midnight Herod signed the decree authorizing the arrest. He knew very well that Jesus could not expect a fair trial before his bitter enemies in Jerusalem.
154.b18.t: First Tiberias conference — Herod refuses to arrest Jesus
The Capernaum synagogue is closed to Jesus
The Sanhedrin decrees all the synagogues of Palestine closed to him
Herod signs the decree authorizing the arrest
Jesus and his company take hasty flight
154.b20.p: That same Saturday night fifty leading citizens of Capernaum met in the synagogue to discuss the question, “⟦Q 154:4.1|168:3.2⟧What shall we do with Jesus?⟦/Q⟧” They debated until after midnight but found no common ground. Apart from a few who thought he might be the Messiah or a prophet, the meeting split into four nearly equal groups.
154.b21.t: A deluded and harmless religious fanatic
A dangerous and designing agitator who might stir up rebellion
One in league with devils, perhaps even a prince of devils
One beside himself, mad, mentally unbalanced
154.b22.p: His enemies said his teachings were impractical, and many well-meaning people in later ages have said that modern civilization could not have been built upon them. But a much better civilization could have been built upon his teachings, and sometime will be.
154.b23.q: ⟦Q 154:4.6⟧This world has never seriously tried to carry out the teachings of Jesus on a large scale⟦/Q⟧
154.b25.p: Before daybreak on May 22 one of David’s messengers arrived from Tiberias with news that Herod had authorized the arrest, and David called an emergency council for seven o’clock. The sister-in-law of Jude, Jesus’ brother, sent word to Jesus’ family and summoned them to the Zebedee house. Knowing that his followers would soon be scattered, Jesus gave them his farewell instructions.
154.b26.t: Seek God for guidance and carry on the work of the kingdom regardless of consequences
Labor as you see fit until you are called
Remain with him no matter what happens
Stay at the Zebedee house and at Peter’s house until he sends for you
Carry on the countrywide messenger service
154.b27.p: David promised that the messengers would never lose contact with him, for he had appointed first and second leaders, even a third, in case anything happened to him. About half past seven Jesus began his parting address to almost one hundred believers. It was a solemn occasion, yet Jesus seemed unusually cheerful, and he inspired them all with words of faith, hope, and courage.
154.b29.p: About eight o’clock Mary, James, Joseph, Jude, and Ruth arrived. Of all his family in the flesh, only Ruth believed wholeheartedly in his mission. His brothers had let pride interfere with their better judgment, and Mary was torn between love and fear, between mother love and family pride. The Pharisees had been working to persuade Mary that Jesus was beside himself, and the family had agreed to try to take him home.
154.b30.p: When Peter whispered that his mother and brothers were outside, Jesus asked that they be told not to fear for him, for the Father would forsake neither him nor his family. Then he stretched out his hands toward the disciples in the room and declared that whoever does the Father’s will is his mother, his brother, and his sister. On hearing these words, Mary collapsed. When a woman cried out that the womb that bore him was blessed, Jesus answered:
154.b31.q: “⟦Q 154:6.7⟧No, rather is the one blessed who hears the word of God and dares to obey it.⟦/Q⟧”
154.b32.p: Jesus did not forsake his family; they forsook him. He did not wish to make their first meeting after so long a separation a public affair in the middle of his address, and he intended to see them afterward. But with word of the coming arrest the company fled in haste, and he never saw his family waiting on the back porch. As he stepped into the boat he asked David to tell them that he appreciated their coming and had intended to see them. All who feel misunderstood or unappreciated have in Jesus a sympathizing friend and an understanding counselor.
154.b34.p: Toward half past eight on the morning of May 22, Jesus, the twelve apostles, and the twelve evangelists rowed for the eastern shore, followed by a smaller boat carrying six of David’s messengers. From now on, for the rest of his earth life, the Master truly “⟦Q 154:7.2⟧had not where to lay his head.⟦/Q⟧” Leaving their boat near Kheresa, they began the wanderings of his last year, going by way of Caesarea-Philippi toward the coast of Phoenicia.
154.b35.p: The Jerusalem officers arrived too late and spent almost a full week vainly searching around Capernaum. His family passed that week in confusion, and found peace only when Ruth learned from David that her brother was safe and well.
154.b37.p: Paper 154 quietly traces how Jesus lost every footing in Capernaum. The synagogues closed, Herod authorized his arrest, the townspeople called him a fanatic, an agitator, or a madman, and even his family tried to take him home. Yet at this lowest point a new following, rooted in spiritual faith, began to grow. Jesus did not heal even his close friends supernaturally, letting souls grow through difficulty, and he called his family not those of his blood but those who do the Father’s will. So he set out on the road of his last year, with nowhere to lay his head.
154.b38.t: At the lowest ebb of popular favor, a healthier faith began to grow
The soul grows not in ease but through difficulty and effort
Herod authorized the arrest, knowing the trial would not be fair
The world has never seriously tried Jesus’ teachings
Jesus urged his scattering followers to carry on regardless of consequences
Those who do the Father’s will are Jesus’ true family
The Master began his last year with nowhere to lay his head
154.b40.box: When everything had turned against him, Jesus made those who do the Father’s will his own family.
155.title: Fleeing Through Northern Galilee
155.b0.ask: “Hunted and on the road, why did Jesus call his apostles to leave the religion of authority and go forward into the religion of the spirit?”
155.b2.p: In Paper 154 we saw the last days at Capernaum and why Jesus had to leave. Paper 155 now follows the flight that came after. Landing near Kheresa, Jesus and the twenty-four spent the night in a park south of Bethsaida-Julias and talked over their plans for a tour through Batanea and northern Galilee to the Phoenician coast.
155.b3.p: On the surface this journey bore little fruit. Few new believers were won, either at Chorazin or at Caesarea-Philippi. Yet it was during this very time that Jesus gave his apostles his deepest teaching on what religion truly is.
155.b4.p: Why, then, on a road of flight, did Jesus call his apostles away from the familiar religion of authority and toward the religion of the spirit, in which each person finds God for himself?
155.b5.q: ⟦Q 155:6.4⟧The religion of the mind ties you hopelessly to the past; the religion of the spirit consists in progressive revelation⟦/Q⟧
155.b8.p: Jesus recalled the Psalm that asks why the heathen rage, and said that the plotting of the rulers was being fulfilled before their eyes. But he corrected the Psalmist’s talk of wrath and a rod of iron as erroneous ideas about the mission of the Son of Man. “⟦Q 155:1.2⟧My kingdom is founded on love, proclaimed in mercy, and established by unselfish service.⟦/Q⟧”
155.b9.t: Enter into the exalted privileges of divine sonship by faith
Kiss the Son, lest he be angry and you perish
Anger and wrath are not a part of establishing the kingdom
155.b10.p: Jesus told them to learn instead from the zeal of their enemies. Because their outlook is narrow, they strike directly for their objectives, while the apostles spent themselves regretting the past, whining over the present, and vainly hoping for the future. He warned them not to become one-sided, and taught that the measure in which truth seekers are drawn to them shows the measure of their own truth endowment, their righteousness.
155.b12.p: Peter went to Chorazin with the twelve evangelists, while Jesus went with the eleven to Caesarea-Philippi. The evangelists said less about healing and preached the spiritual truths of the kingdom with new vigor, yet no city in all Galilee yielded so few souls. These two weeks were a veritable baptism of adversity, the most difficult and unproductive time of their careers, and because of it each one took stock more earnestly and honestly of his own soul.
155.b13.p: When they rejoined Jesus at Caesarea-Philippi on June 8, he spoke again of the parable of the sower and taught them much about the meaning of the apparent failure of life undertakings.
155.b15.p: These two weeks were a real test for the apostles, who were well-nigh depressed. Yet they learned much from their daily conferences with the Master. They learned that when truth becomes a boundary line of self-righteous exclusiveness instead of a signpost of spiritual progress, it loses its life-giving power and becomes fossilizing. And they learned that many souls can best be led to love the unseen God by first being taught to love their brethren whom they can see.
155.b16.q: ⟦Q 155:3.5⟧true religion was man’s heartfelt loyalty to his highest and truest convictions.⟦/Q⟧
155.b17.p: If a person’s religious longings are only material, growing knowledge of nature will in the end take away his faith in God; but if his religion is spiritual, the progress of science can never disturb his faith in eternal realities. Jesus’ whole earth life was devoted to thawing out the frozen forms of religion into the liquid liberties of enlightened sonship.
155.b18.t: Supposed supernatural explanations are displaced, and faith in God is lost
Faith in eternal realities and divine values is never disturbed
155.b20.p: On June 9 the twenty-five teachers of truth left Caesarea-Philippi for the road to Sidon. As they paused for lunch in the shadow of a ledge of rock near Luz, Peter asked why they fled from their enemies instead of confronting them. Thomas broke in to ask what the real difference was between their religion and that of the leaders at Jerusalem, when all professed to serve the same God. Jesus said it would help them more if he answered Thomas’s question, and he promised to do so after lunch.
155.b22.p: The religions of the world have a double origin, natural and revelatory, and among any people at any time three distinct forms of religious devotion are found side by side.
155.b23.t: The urge to fear mysterious energies — the religion of the physical nature, the religion of fear
Intellectual theology resting on the authority of tradition — the religion of the mind
3. True religion, the religion of revelation
The religion of the spirit as demonstrated in human experience
155.b24.p: The great difference between the religion of the mind and the religion of the spirit is that the first is upheld by ecclesiastical authority, while the second is wholly based on human experience. The religion of authority offers a ready refuge to a soul harassed by fear, but its price is the sovereignty of personality and the supreme adventure of man seeking God for himself and finding him.
155.b25.q: ⟦Q 155:5.11⟧The religion of the spirit means effort, struggle, conflict, faith, determination, love, loyalty, and progress.⟦/Q⟧
155.b26.p: Then Jesus pointed to each of the twenty-four and called them by name. Would they go back to the easy path of traditional authority, or go forward with him into an uncertain and troublous future? When they rose to their feet, deeply moved, he raised his hand to stop them and told each one to go apart alone with the Father and find there the unemotional answer to his question.
155.b28.p: In the afternoon, in the shade of a hillside, Jesus went on teaching. The Father did not stop speaking words of truth when the prophets of old ended their utterances. “⟦Q 155:6.2⟧Commit not the folly of calling that divine which is wholly human,⟦/Q⟧” he said, and learn to discern truths that do not come through the traditional channels. To be born again is to pass from a faith inherited to a personal faith achieved by actual experience, from a theology of mind to a true religion of spirit.
155.b29.t: Unity of experience, with full allowance for diversity of belief
Divides men and sets them against each other
Draws men together in understanding sympathy
Ties you hopelessly to the past
Beckons you on through progressive revelation
A present feeling of settled security
Freedom to follow the truth wherever the spirit leads
Grows in loving service and merciful ministration
155.b30.p: Every race has its own mental outlook, so the religions of authority can never come to unification; human brotherhood can be reached only through the religion of the spirit, for all mankind is indwelt by the same divine spirit. Jesus also warned them not to look down on the children of Abraham, for Israel’s long and untiring struggle to find God had prepared the way for the greater revelation they were now called to share.
155.b31.q: ⟦Q 155:6.12⟧It is not so important that you should know about the fact of God as that you should increasingly grow in the ability to feel the presence of God.⟦/Q⟧
155.b32.p: The will of God can be done in any earthly occupation, and all things are sacred in the lives of those who are spirit led. Jesus told them not to try to prove to others that they had found God, and named two positive demonstrations of it.
155.b33.t: The fruits of the spirit of God showing forth in daily life
A life that has risked everything it is and has on the adventure of survival
155.b34.p: The Father responds to the faintest flicker of faith, even to the superstitious emotions of primitive man or the feeble assent of fearful souls to a religion of authority. But the apostles, called out of darkness into the light, were to believe with a whole heart, in body, mind, and spirit. Their religion was to be the fact of real experience, testifying that God had found them and that they had enlisted in the eternal adventure of finding him.
155.b36.p: Paper 155 shows that the deepest teaching was given in the middle of a journey that looked like failure. The hardships of Chorazin and the gloom of Caesarea-Philippi led the apostles to examine their own souls, and on the road to Phoenicia Jesus asked them to choose between the easy way and the hard one. The religion of authority gives security, but it binds people to the past and divides them. The religion of the spirit is an uncertain adventure, but it lets each person find God and joins different people into one. What Jesus wanted was not an emotional outburst but a quiet and sincere answer, found alone before the Father.
155.b37.t: The kingdom is built not on wrath but on love, mercy, and service
Fruitless adversity leads one to take stock of one’s own soul
Truth hardened into a creed becomes fossilized; spiritual religion is not shaken
Jesus answered first the question of how religions differ
Choose between the easy path of authority and the hard adventure of the spirit
The religion of the spirit unites people through unity of experience, not of belief
155.b39.box: True religion is not inherited authority but the living experience of finding God for oneself and of being found by him.
156.title: The Sojourn at Tyre and Sidon
156.b0.ask: “In those weeks in Phoenicia, when he seemed to have been driven out, what did Jesus sow among the gentiles, and what did he teach?”
156.b2.p: In Paper 155, on the road to Phoenicia, Jesus contrasted the religion of authority with the religion of the spirit and called his apostles to choose the harder way. Paper 156 tells of the days at the end of that road, in Sidon and Tyre. Arriving near Sidon on June 10, the company spent a quiet Sabbath turning over the discourses they had heard on the way, though none of them fully grasped their meaning.
156.b3.p: In Galilee the synagogues were closed and hostility ran high, but the gentiles of Phoenicia gladly received the gospel. These six weeks or so were a very fruitful time in the work of winning souls.
156.b4.p: What, then, did Jesus sow among the gentiles during this time when he seemed to have been driven away, and what did he teach his apostles?
156.b5.q: “⟦Q 156:2.1⟧This world is only a bridge; you may pass over it, but you should not think to build a dwelling place upon it.⟦/Q⟧”
156.b8.p: While Jesus was resting at the home of Karuska, a Syrian woman named Norana came with her twelve-year-old daughter, who suffered from convulsions. She believed that her child was possessed by an unclean spirit. The apostles, wanting the Master to rest, tried one after another to send her away, but Norana would not give an inch.
156.b9.t: Who tried to send her away
She would not leave until she had seen the Master
Why would his disciples send away those who come seeking his help?
Even the dogs may have the crumbs that fall from the children’s table
156.b10.p: Jesus, who had heard everything through an open window, came out and said that her faith was so great that he could not withhold what she desired; her daughter had already been made whole. The next day he told his apostles to see how gentiles could exercise saving faith, and warned that the Father’s kingdom would be taken by the gentiles if the children of Abraham did not show faith enough to enter it.
156.b12.p: As they entered Sidon they crossed a bridge, the first many of them had ever seen, and Jesus said that this world is only a bridge to pass over, not a place to build a dwelling. Each morning he taught the twenty-four at the home of Justa, and in the afternoons and evenings they went out to preach in the city.
156.b13.p: In many ways these gentile believers understood Jesus more fully than the Jews did. They came to know not only that Jesus was like God but also that God was like Jesus. They grasped that there is no favoritism with the Universal Father, and that the universe is law-abiding and unfailingly dependable.
156.b14.q: ⟦Q 156:2.4⟧All down through the ages men have not been unable to comprehend Jesus; they have been afraid to.⟦/Q⟧
156.b15.p: The theme of his teaching in Sidon was spiritual progression. They could not stand still; they must go forward in righteousness or slide back into evil. His disciples were not only to cease doing evil but to learn to do well; confessed sins are forgiven, so they should not harbor feelings of guilt but keep a conscience void of offense. Jesus greatly enjoyed the gentiles’ sense of humor, and regretted that his own people took themselves too seriously.
156.b17.p: On June 28 the company left Sidon and went up the coast. The apostles preached in Porphyreon and the evangelists taught in Heldua, and many were added to the kingdom. Meanwhile Jesus went alone to Beirut to visit Malach, a believer.
156.b18.p: By the time they reached Tyre on July 11, the apostles and evangelists had grown used to working among these so-called gentiles, who were mainly descended from Canaanite tribes of earlier Semitic origin and spoke Greek. Their eagerness to hear the gospel and their readiness to believe greatly surprised the apostles.
156.b20.p: From July 11 to July 24 the apostles and evangelists, two by two, taught throughout Tyre and its environs, and many were baptized. Jesus made his headquarters at the home of Joseph, a believer, south of the city. He spoke in Tyre only once, on July 20, teaching the Father’s love for all mankind, and on that occasion the doors of the Melkarth temple were opened to him.
156.b21.p: Many of the leaders in the making of Tyrian purple believed in the kingdom. When the shellfish that were the source of the dye began to diminish, these dye makers went out in search of new habitats, and migrating to the ends of the earth, they carried with them the message of the fatherhood of God and the brotherhood of man.
156.b23.p: Jesus told the story of the white lily, which lifts its pure head into the sunshine while its roots are grounded in the dark muck below. In the same way, mortal man, though rooted in the animal soil of human nature, can by faith raise his spiritual nature into the sunlight of heavenly truth. In his only parable drawn from carpentry, he warned against wasting time squaring and smoothing worm-eaten timber, and urged them to build foundations of character able to support the growing spiritual nature.
156.b24.p: Nathaniel asked why we pray not to be led into temptation, when God never does such things. Jesus answered that their forefathers saw the hand of God in everything, but that men are all too often led into temptation by their own selfishness and the impulses of their animal natures. Then he contrasted two ways of meeting temptation.
156.b25.t: Holding desire down by the mere force of the human will
One is more and more overburdened by suppressed desires
Coming truly to love the higher forms of conduct
One is delivered through spiritual transformation, and the old is forgotten
156.b26.q: ⟦Q 156:5.5⟧There is mighty power in the expulsive energy of a new and sincere spiritual affection.⟦/Q⟧
156.b27.p: The questions went on long into the night, and Jesus gave them many teachings about the life of a believer.
156.b28.t: It may tend toward evil, but it is not inherently sinful
Mistakes you fail to forget in time will be forgotten in eternity
Not by a single unfortunate episode, but by spiritual longings and purposes
Divine love is outgoing; it cannot be self-bestowed
It is not self-admiration; it grows with the love and service of one’s fellows
The ability to resist holding grudges and to withstand brooding in sorrow
Tact is the fulcrum of social leverage; tolerance is the earmark of a great soul
Render to Caesar the things that are material, and to God those that are spiritual
156.b29.p: The day before leaving Tyre, Jesus directed the twelve evangelists to return by a different route, and after that they were never again so intimately associated with him.
156.b31.p: On July 24 Jesus and the twelve set out by way of Ptolemais, Jotapata, Ramah, and Zebulun to Gennesaret, and then crossed the lake. In the park where the five thousand had been fed, they held conferences with about fifty believers, the remnant of the once numerous company at Capernaum.
156.b32.p: While Jesus was away, things had changed a great deal. His enemies thought the movement was broken up and let their opposition subside, and the tried and true survivors of the great sifting began to gather again. Now the issues of battle were clearly drawn, and the reorganization for his last year began.
156.b33.t: Sent word that Jesus was free to live and work in his domains
Resented the closing of the synagogues and turned against the Sanhedrin leaders
Secretly opened their synagogues to Abner and his associates
Let it be known that he had not authorized Jesus’ arrest outside Galilee, in Perea
156.b35.p: Paper 156 shows that what looked like a retreat was really a season of sowing. A gentile woman’s persistent and good-humored faith moved Jesus’ heart, the people of Sidon and Tyre received the gospel without fear, and the dye makers carried its message to the ends of the earth. Meanwhile Jesus taught his apostles about spiritual progress, the true way to overcome temptation, and a life that grows more skillful in love each day. When they returned, the situation in Galilee had changed, and with the sifted believers the road of the final year was opening.
156.b36.t: A gentile’s persistent, good-humored faith brought healing
The world is only a bridge; do not stand still but go forward
The gentiles longed for the gospel and readily believed
The dye makers carried the gospel to the ends of the earth
Temptation is overcome not by suppression but by a higher love
With the sifted believers, the reorganization for the final year began
156.b38.box: As the lily rooted in the mud lifts its flower toward the light, so man by faith bears the fruits of the spirit.
157.title: At Caesarea-Philippi
157.b0.ask: “Why did Peter’s answer to the question ‘Who say you that I am?’ open a new epoch in Jesus’ life?”
157.b2.p: In Paper 156 Jesus and the apostles finished their mission in Phoenicia, returned to Galilee, and began gathering their scattered forces. Paper 157 follows their short journey to Caesarea-Philippi. Before it, Jesus had arranged to meet his family at Capernaum on August 7, but Pharisees from Jerusalem installed themselves in Mary’s home, and the meeting never took place. And so again, through no fault of either, Jesus and his earth family failed to make contact.
157.b3.p: At the heart of this paper is a question asked under the mulberry trees. For three years Jesus had called himself the Son of Man; now, for the first time, he asked his apostles who he himself was.
157.b4.p: What, then, was new in Peter’s confession, and why did it become the door to the last stage of Jesus’ life?
157.b5.q: “⟦Q 157:4.5⟧Upon this rock of spiritual reality will I build the living temple of spiritual fellowship in the eternal realities of my Father’s kingdom.⟦/Q⟧”
157.b8.p: While they waited by the lake, a temple-tax collector took Peter aside and asked whether his Master did not pay the temple tax. Seeing that it was a trap, Peter hastily promised to bring the tax at once, though in fact they had no money with them. Jesus said that if Peter had promised, he should pay, and that it was well to pay so as to give the authorities no occasion for offense; Peter was to catch some fish and sell them.
157.b9.p: A messenger of David who had overheard everything, and his fisherman friend, handed Peter several large baskets of fish and added to the price, so that the tax for all three could be paid. As Peter left, Jesus remarked half-humorously that perhaps he would catch the fish with the shekel in its mouth. Since stories of treasure found in the mouths of fish were common in those days, the episode was later expanded into a miracle.
157.b11.p: At Magadan Park, more than one hundred believers gathered, and Pharisees and Sadducees came too, demanding a sign of his authority. Jesus asked how it was that they could discern the face of the heavens but not the signs of the times, and said that to an evil-minded and hypocritical generation no sign would be given.
157.b12.p: At the evening conference it was decided to undertake a united mission through the Decapolis on their return. Jesus warned them to beware of the leaven of the Pharisees and the Sadducees: it is not the fear of a dead religion that saves, but faith in a living experience. When love for a neighbor wells up in the heart, it should not be stifled but expressed in intelligent ministry to real needs.
157.b13.q: ⟦Q 157:2.2⟧It is not the purpose of true religion merely to bring peace but rather to insure progress.⟦/Q⟧
157.b15.p: As he entered the final epoch of his work, Jesus wished to return to Mount Hermon, the mount of his trial and triumph, hoping the apostles might gain a new vision and new strength there. When they paused for lunch under the mulberry trees, he asked them the first question he had ever addressed to them concerning himself: “⟦Q 157:3.3⟧Who do men say that I am?⟦/Q⟧”
157.b16.t: A prophet or an extraordinary man
One in league with the prince of devils
Some who had not met him
John the Baptist risen from the dead
One compared with Moses, Elijah, Isaiah, and Jeremiah
The Deliverer, the Son of the living God
157.b17.p: Jesus rose and asked, “⟦Q 157:3.5⟧But who say you that I am?⟦/Q⟧” After a moment of tense silence Peter sprang to his feet, and the other eleven rose with one accord. Jesus told them that this had been revealed to them by his Father, and charged them for the time being to tell no man. That night the apostles slept little; they sensed that a great event had taken place.
157.b19.p: For a long time the apostles had been in turmoil between the Messiah they held in their minds and the extraordinary man they knew in their hearts. The next day, in Celsus’ garden, Jesus asked whether, now that a full day had passed, they still held to their decision. Peter answered again, “⟦Q 157:4.4⟧We believe that you are the Son of the living God.⟦/Q⟧” After that day the twelve never again greeted their Master by rising when he came into their presence.
157.b20.p: Jesus said that this belief was not mere human knowledge but a revelation of his Father’s spirit to their inmost souls, and that upon this foundation he would build the brotherhood of the kingdom of heaven. The guidance of the spirit fellowship he left to his Father’s spirit, but to the apostles he delivered the keys of the outward kingdom, authority over its social and economic affairs. On this day the Master began to believe in the faith of his apostles, save one.
157.b21.t: Guidance and teaching of the spirit fellowship
The keys of the outward kingdom (social and economic affairs)
157.b23.p: The new and vital feature of Peter’s confession was the clear-cut recognition that Jesus was the Son of God. The Jews expected the Messiah to be “⟦Q 157:5.1|98:7.2|136:1.1⟧the anointed one,⟦/Q⟧” but they had hardly thought of him as “⟦Q 157:4.5|157:5.1|157:5.3⟧the Son of God,⟦/Q⟧” springing from divinity. Seeing that his plan to modify their idea of the Messiah could hardly succeed, Jesus chose a third plan: openly to announce his divinity.
157.b24.t: A national deliverer, an anointed man
The Son of God — recognition of his divinity
Son of Man and Son of God — his combined nature
157.b25.p: Upon the truth of this combined nature, Son of Man and Son of God, Jesus determined to build the kingdom of heaven. He gave up trying to convince the apostles that he was not the Messiah, and resolved boldly to reveal to them what he is.
157.b27.p: After his popularity collapsed the treasury was empty, but David Zebedee had foreseen this and had his messengers collect money, and enough funds arrived. The apostles little realized that this was the beginning of a new epoch in their Master’s career, yet from this time on a new note appeared in his message.
157.b28.t: Stage of his life in the flesh
Only dimly conscious of his origin, nature, and destiny
Growing understanding of his divine nature and mission, up to his baptism
From the baptism to Peter’s confession — known as the Son of Man
From Caesarea-Philippi to the crucifixion — the acknowledgment of divinity
157.b29.p: Before Caesarea-Philippi Jesus presented the gospel as its master teacher; after it he appeared as the divine representative of the eternal Father, and yet he had to do all this as a human being, the Son of Man. He did not stress an incessant struggle between soul and body, but taught that the spirit is easy victor over both and reconciles them.
157.b30.p: In the garden the apostles heard startling words: let any who would have fellowship with us assume the obligations of sonship and follow me; the Son of Man came not to be ministered to but to minister; before Abraham was, I am; the Father and I are one. The apostles were stunned and went off in small groups to ponder them, still unable to grasp the full meaning of their own confession.
157.b31.q: “⟦Q 157:6.13|169:4.12|180:3.9⟧He who has seen me has seen the Father.⟦/Q⟧”
157.b33.p: That evening Andrew had searching talks with each of his brethren, but he was so worried by Judas Iscariot’s attitude that late at night he went to Jesus. Jesus answered that there was nothing more they could do; Andrew should go on placing the utmost confidence in this apostle and say nothing to the others about their talk.
157.b34.t: The death of John the Baptist
Jesus’ refusal to be made king
Refusing the challenge for a sign
157.b35.p: The other apostles faced the same trials, but they loved Jesus and went through with him to the bitter end. The great mistake of Judas was that, whenever Jesus sent the apostles off to pray, he indulged in thoughts of human fear instead of sincere communion with the spiritual forces of the universe, and harbored doubts and feelings of revenge. On August 12 Jesus told the twelve to prepare for a journey to the mountain, where the spirit bade him go to be endowed for the finish of his work on earth.
157.b37.p: Paper 157 shows a hinge in Jesus’ life. People thought him a prophet or John risen from the dead, but Peter, by the insight of the spirit, confessed him as the Son of the living God. Jesus declared that on the rock of that confession he would build a living temple of spiritual fellowship, and from then on he revealed himself as Son of Man and Son of God as he entered his last year. Yet in the same company the heart of Judas was turning toward fear and resentment. Two people may pass through the same experiences, and what each communes with in prayer decides the path he takes.
157.b38.t: He kept his word to avoid giving offense, and the story later became a miracle
Discern the signs of the times, not demanded signs, and trust living experience
Beyond popular opinion, Peter confessed the Deliverer, the Son of God
On the rock of a revealed confession the spiritual brotherhood is built
Not merely the Messiah, but Son of Man and Son of God
Jesus’ life entered its last stage, the revelation of his divinity
Instead of praying, Judas gave way to fear and doubt
157.b40.box: Jesus, Son of Man and Son of God, builds the living temple of sonship on the rock of a confession revealed by the spirit.
158.title: The Mount of Transfiguration
158.b0.ask: “Between the glory on the mountain and the defeat below it, why did Jesus choose to carry his bestowal through to the end, and begin to speak to his followers of his death?”
158.b2.p: In Paper 157 Peter confessed Jesus as the Son of the living God, and Jesus entered the last stage of his life. Paper 158 tells what happened on Mount Hermon six days after that confession. On August 12 the company reached the foot of the mountain, the very place where Jesus had once gone up alone to settle the spiritual destinies of Urantia and technically to end the Lucifer rebellion.
158.b3.p: Jesus wished all his apostles could share this experience, but they could not attain the spiritual levels needed to witness the full visitation of the celestial beings. So he took only Peter, James, and John, the three who usually went with him when he withdrew to pray alone.
158.b4.p: Glory awaited on the mountain, and defeat below it. Why, between the two, did Jesus refuse full authority and choose to carry his bestowal to the end, and why did he now begin to tell his followers of his death?
158.b5.q: “⟦Q 158:1.10|158:3.4⟧This is my beloved Son; give heed to him.⟦/Q⟧”
158.b8.p: On August 15 Jesus climbed Mount Hermon with the three apostles. It is significant that this event took place in the lands of the gentiles, on a mountain of the gentiles. That day Jesus could have relinquished the struggle and returned to the rule of his universe, but he chose to meet the last and full measure of his Father’s will. The three apostles saw him decline to be invested with full universe authority and watched as he was left alone to finish his earth life.
158.b9.t: The feeding of the five thousand
At a high point, then falling almost to zero
The weeks after he admitted his divinity
Rising to its highest pitch, then steadily declining
158.b10.p: About three in the afternoon Jesus went apart for a long conference with Gabriel and the Father Melchizedek. That night the three apostles awoke to see Jesus, shining with a heavenly light, talking with two brilliant beings; Peter mistakenly took them for Moses and Elijah. As Peter, in his confusion, offered to put up three tents, a silvery cloud overshadowed them, and they heard the same voice that had spoken at Jesus’ baptism.
158.b11.q: “⟦Q 158:1.10⟧Arise and be not afraid; you shall see greater things than this.⟦/Q⟧”
158.b13.p: Jesus told them to tell no one what they had seen until the Son of Man had risen from the dead. Having just seen him in glory, the apostles were shocked by the words “⟦Q 158:2.1|158:7.7⟧rising from the dead.⟦/Q⟧” To avoid the subject, Peter asked about Elijah, and Jesus answered that Elijah had already come and had not been received, referring to John the Baptist.
158.b14.p: Jesus asked for silence because he did not want to encourage the mistaken idea of a wonder-working deliverer. Since they would not receive him as the Son of Man, he had consented to be received according to their settled determination, but he warned that this choice would bring them many disappointments. The three were not chosen because they were better prepared, but because they were the ones assigned to go with him when he sought solitary communion.
158.b16.p: What the three apostles saw was only a fleeting glimpse of a celestial pageant that took place on Mount Hermon that day. The transfiguration was the occasion of these testimonies.
158.b17.t: Assurance that the requirements of the Eternal Son had been fulfilled
Satisfaction with the fullness of the bestowal in mortal flesh
“⟦Q 158:1.10|158:3.4⟧This is my beloved Son; give heed to him⟦/Q⟧”
158.b18.p: Jesus welcomed these testimonies, but he noted that his Father did not indicate that the bestowal was finished. So he decided to pursue the mortal bestowal to its natural end. This was the meaning of the transfiguration to Jesus; to the apostles it marked the Master’s entrance upon the final phase of his career on earth.
158.b20.p: In the camp below, a crowd of about fifty, the nine apostles together with Jerusalem scribes and believing disciples, was loudly disputing. James of Safed had just arrived after searching for Jesus for nearly two weeks, bringing his only son of about fourteen, who was epileptic and also possessed by a wandering midwayer. When he came, the nine apostles were arguing about who should be greatest in the coming kingdom.
158.b21.p: Simon Zelotes and Judas Iscariot stepped forward, declaring that the keys of the kingdom had been delivered to them, and commanded the spirit to come out; but the boy only had a more violent fit, and the scribes mocked them. Andrew, after prayer, tried a second time and also failed. He frankly confessed defeat and asked the father to wait until the Master returned.
158.b23.p: The father knelt at Jesus’ feet and poured out the story of his son’s suffering. Jesus said that the works of faith do not come forth at the bidding of doubting unbelief, and told the father not to question the Father’s power of love but only the sincerity of his own faith. Then James of Safed spoke words long to be remembered: “⟦Q 158:5.2⟧Lord, I believe. I pray you help my unbelief.⟦/Q⟧”
158.b24.p: Saying he would act in accordance with his Father’s will and in honor of living faith, Jesus raised the boy and placed the lad’s hand in his father’s. This was a true healing of a double affliction, physical and spiritual, and the boy was permanently cured from that hour.
158.b25.t: The spiritual ecstasy of the transfiguration
Failure, humiliation, and a sleepless night
158.b26.p: To come straight from such ecstasy to the scene of their brethren’s defeat was a disillusionment, but it was ever so with these twelve: they alternated between exaltation and humiliation.
158.b28.p: When Thomas asked to be taught about their failure, Jesus pointed out that those who stayed behind, instead of praying, had fallen into their old temptation of seeking preferred places in the kingdom. Spiritual greatness consists in an understanding love that is Godlike, not in enjoying the exercise of material power.
158.b29.t: What went wrong in their attempt
Not the will of the Father in heaven
158.b30.p: Spiritual work cannot be done without spiritual power, and even where that potential is present, the personal experience of living faith is needed. Then Jesus declared that the Son of Man would be put to death but would rise again, and the apostles went to bed sorrowful and bewildered.
158.b32.p: The next day, on the road, Andrew asked whether Jesus was speaking in parables. Jesus answered plainly that he was not: he must go to Jerusalem, be rejected, be killed, and be raised from the dead. Out of love, Peter declared that these things would never happen to him.
158.b33.p: Jesus recognized in those affectionate words the subtle suggestion of temptation to turn aside from his Father’s will, and he rebuked him sharply: “⟦Q 158:7.4|53:8.4⟧Get you behind me,⟦/Q⟧” and “⟦Q 158:7.4⟧Mind not the ways of men but rather the will of God.⟦/Q⟧” He was always patient with human shortcomings, but not when the program of doing his Father’s will was threatened.
158.b34.q: ⟦Q 158:7.5⟧What does it profit a man to gain the whole world and lose his own soul?⟦/Q⟧
158.b35.p: Jesus was not sending them alone into the conflict; he was leading them, and he asked only that they bravely follow. Not one of them was minded to forsake him, but his words about rising from the dead utterly failed to register in their minds.
158.b37.p: At Peter’s house in Capernaum Jesus asked what they had been discussing so earnestly that afternoon, and they held their peace, for they had again been arguing about who should be greatest. Jesus set one of Peter’s little children among them and said that whoever humbles himself and becomes as this little one shall be greatest in the kingdom of heaven.
158.b38.p: To be first in the kingdom, they were to minister these truths to their brethren, to sacrifice the cherished idols that hinder the kingdom’s progress, and above all to despise not one of these little ones.
158.b40.p: Paper 158 sets the glory on the mountain beside the reality below it. On Mount Hermon Jesus received testimony that his bestowal had been fulfilled, yet he declined full authority and chose to carry out his Father’s will to the end. Below, the apostles were still quarreling over rank, and commands given without faith accomplished nothing. Jesus helped a father’s wavering faith and healed his son, and he rejected even Peter’s loving protest as a temptation. With the teaching that the greatest is the one who humbles himself like a little child, Jesus set out on the last road toward his death and resurrection.
158.b41.t: Even in glory he declined full authority and remained alone
After the vision of glory he first spoke of death and resurrection
Though attested, he chose to carry the bestowal to its natural end
Commands from apostles caught up in rivalry had no power
He answered an honest faith that asked help for its unbelief
Spiritual work requires pure motives and living faith
Not even a loving protest may stand in the way of the Father’s will
The one who humbles himself like a child is the greatest
158.b43.box: On the mountain of glory Jesus laid authority aside and came down to walk the way of doing the Father’s will to the end.
